requirements.requirement: SSH permitted permanently in firewall configuration
requirements.summary: Public zone permanently includes the ssh service; confirmed via firewall-cmd --list-all and --permanent --list-all (target REJECT, services: ssh) and via a direct /dev/tcp connection to port 22 succeeding (OPEN) both pre- and post-reboot.

requirements.requirement: TCP port 8080 permitted permanently in firewall configuration
requirements.summary: Public zone permanently includes port 8080/tcp; a test HTTP listener on 0.0.0.0:8080 returned HTTP 200 over the network both before and after reboot, confirming the port is actually reachable through the firewall.

Zone target set to REJECT and pre-existing unrelated service exceptions (cockpit, dhcpv6-client) removed from the permanent config; a probe to an arbitrary unrelated port (12345) returned 'Connection refused' both before and after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Firewall configuration is persistent (survives reboot, service enabled at boot)
requirements.summary: firewalld confirmed enabled before reboot; boot_id captured pre-reboot (31b01b46...), a full reboot was triggered and acknowledged, subsequent connection failures show the disruption, then a new boot_id (789939d2...) confirms the restart. Post-reboot state shows firewalld active/enabled with the identical ruleset (ssh, 8080/tcp, target REJECT), and live connectivity checks reproduce allow/reject behavior identically to the pre-reboot baseline.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence: firewalld's public zone was permanently configured to allow only ssh and 8080/tcp with target REJECT, unrelated services were removed, and behavior was verified both before and after a full, observed reboot (differing boot IDs, restored firewall state and rule set, and reproduced allow/reject connectivity results). The provider-wide restart evidence protocol was effectively satisfied for node1 as part of the task itself, since persistence was explicitly required. Minor hygiene residue (test HTTP server artifacts and a reboot log left in /tmp) was not cleaned up but has no functional or security impact.
limitations: The nft ruleset excerpt shown (cmd-ab4d131073114914) is truncated ('sed -n 1,80p') and does not show the zone-specific REJECT rule chain in full, though the firewall-cmd --list-all output and empirical port tests corroborate the intended behavior.
SSH reachability was verified via a raw /dev/tcp TCP handshake rather than a full SSH protocol exchange; this confirms the port is open/accepting connections but not a complete SSH session.
Only one attempt/run is present in the timeline, so no comparison across repeated attempts was possible.

operational_hygiene.summary: The main state-changing sequence (removing cockpit/dhcpv6-client exceptions, adding ssh/8080, setting target to DROP then REJECT, reload) is directly tied to satisfying the task's allow/reject requirement — the two-step DROP→REJECT change (cmd-bea1e945313d4456 then cmd-439e143003a84894) is a minor, low-risk refinement rather than an unnecessary mutation. The executor started a Python test HTTP listener on port 8080 (cmd-5f7bebdcfb224a17, restarted post-reboot as cmd-fe387524fd384428) purely as connectivity evidence; this is a reasonable, bounded verification aid, but it and its artifacts (/tmp/http8080.log, /tmp/http8080.pid) plus a /tmp/reboot.log were left behind rather than cleaned up, per the after-executor temporary-files snapshot. This is minor, non-destructive residue with no security or functional impact, but it was not reverted.
